The pages switch at once and the tray brings the open UI forward instead of another tab; the verdicts page shows any network's verdicts and resets that one only; the core is the fork at upstream Alpha with its API and listeners locked down; and a review's worth of security fixes.

To update, run the new `dpiswitch.exe` from anywhere and accept the offer to install over the installed version (one administrator prompt). Settings, lists, configs and verdicts are kept.

## Interface

- **The pages switch at once.** Every page is kept in one document, fetched once and kept laid out while away; the menu and a page's own tabs (the verdicts' kinds, the logs) switch on the press of the button, not on its release. From the press to the page on screen: 4-7 ms, Live 15, Verdicts 23-28 — a page load was 55-140 ms after the click, and the click comes a quarter of a second after the press.
- **The tray brings the open UI forward instead of opening another tab.** The UI opens in a window of its own — an app window of the default browser when it is Chrome, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi or Yandex Browser — and that window is found again by its title. A browser window whose tab shown is the UI comes forward too.
- **Verdicts' rows work as Live's:** a click picks a row, a right-click sends its whole domain, name or address to a list or a preset, ✕ resets that one verdict. Rows on both pages are picked as the button goes down.
- **Live says how long ago the core started**, beside the traffic counted since. A paused table has no close buttons: it shows the past.
- **The tunnels' state follows the traffic, every second:** the tray's icon, the header, the overview and the second tunnel's page. A dead tunnel stayed green for up to 40 seconds. The state speaks Russian too.
- **The pages speak the tray's language** until switched, not the browser's.

## Verdicts and networks

- **The verdicts page shows any network kept.** On it the network in the header opens the list of networks; the one picked has its verdicts shown, and the reset and ✕ act on it alone. Leaving the page goes back to the current network.
- **A reset is of one network.** The page's button resets the network shown, the tray's "Everything via tunnel" the current one; both used to drop the verdicts of every network.
- **Another network's verdicts age:** a network nothing has gone through for a month goes whole. An ISP met once kept its verdicts for good.
- **Started offline, nothing is filed under no network:** the last list stays until the network is found. What an offline start filed used to be applied on whatever network came next.

## Core and tunnels

- **The core is the fork at upstream Alpha 9f053c49,** its API narrowed to what the service calls.
- **The prober's listeners take its own user only.** Any program of any account could go past the tunnel through them; UDP now goes only through an association that signed in.
- **The core runs from Program Files**, beside the program, not from inside its data directory.
- **The IPv6 check restarts the core instead of re-reading its config in place,** which left two WireGuard sessions with one key and dropped the tunnel for minutes; "no IPv6 here" is held for a day.
- **The core's API secret is read again when the core refuses it:** after a config was written anew the controller saw nothing and the health check restarted the core every minute.
- **A failed ISP lookup pauses for ten minutes** instead of taking most of every minute.
- **The tray's icon comes back when Explorer restarts.**

## DNS

- **The default resolvers for direct sites are Google's DoT** (`tls://8.8.8.8`, `tls://8.8.4.4`), in place of Yandex's DoH and DoT. Resolvers set in the settings stay as they are.
- A DoH address keeps its query string: the test asked another URL than the core.

## Security

- **The data directory is read by its owner,** SYSTEM and the administrators, not by every account: the core's log names every host the machine connects to.
- **The owner is the one recorded at install,** never guessed from old files' permissions.
- **A second name of a file elsewhere, planted in the data directory, is removed,** not given the service's permissions.
- **The service does not start in a data directory it could not lock down.**
- **Windows' own programs are run by their full path,** not looked up along PATH.
- **The UI's requests to drop verdicts are read as the user's files,** never through a link, and written whole.
- golang.org/x/crypto 0.57.0.

## Fixes

- A direct list whose old programs' file cannot go is not saved: it would go on routing them.
- A preset's two files no longer part when the settings cannot be written.
- `example.com:abc` is no longer taken for `example.com`.
